facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Auguste Comte
facts.summary: French philosopher who coined the word sociology and held that society should be studied by the positive methods of the natural sciences.
facts.verified: books: Anthony Giddens; IGNOU Sociology Paper 1

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Karl Marx
facts.summary: German thinker whose historical materialism explains society through its mode of production and the struggle between classes.
facts.verified: books: Haralambos & Holborn; IGNOU Sociology Paper 1

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Friedrich Engels
facts.summary: Marx's lifelong collaborator and co-author of The Communist Manifesto, who traced the family and the state to private property.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Émile Durkheim
facts.summary: French founder of academic sociology who treated social facts as things and explained social order through solidarity and the collective conscience.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Max Weber
facts.summary: German sociologist of interpretive understanding who studied social action, authority, bureaucracy and the part religion played in the rise of capitalism.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Talcott Parsons
facts.summary: American structural functionalist who built a general theory of action and of society as a social system.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Robert K. Merton
facts.summary: American functionalist who refined functional analysis and proposed middle-range theory, reference group theory and a structural theory of deviance.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: George Herbert Mead
facts.summary: American pragmatist philosopher whose account of the self, symbols and role-taking became the basis of symbolic interactionism.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Charles Horton Cooley
facts.summary: American sociologist who described the looking-glass self and the primary group.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Herbert Blumer
facts.summary: American sociologist, a student of Mead, who named and systematised symbolic interactionism.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Erving Goffman
facts.summary: Canadian-born American sociologist who analysed face-to-face interaction through the dramaturgical metaphor of performance.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: C. Wright Mills
facts.summary: American critical sociologist who wrote on the sociological imagination and on the power elite in the United States.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Bronisław Malinowski
facts.summary: Polish-born British anthropologist who pioneered long-term fieldwork and participant observation in the Trobriand Islands.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Claude Lévi-Strauss
facts.summary: French structural anthropologist whose alliance theory explains kinship through marriage exchange between groups.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: George Peter Murdock
facts.summary: American anthropologist whose cross-cultural survey in Social Structure (1949) argued that the nuclear family is universal.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Kingsley Davis
facts.summary: American sociologist and demographer who, with Wilbert Moore, proposed the functionalist theory of stratification.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Pitirim Sorokin
facts.summary: Russian-American sociologist whose Social Mobility (1927) was the first systematic study of movement between social positions.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Vilfredo Pareto
facts.summary: Italian economist and sociologist of elite theory, known for the circulation of elites.
facts.verified: books: Haralambos & Holborn; IGNOU Sociology Paper 1

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Robert Michels
facts.summary: German-born sociologist whose study of socialist parties led to the iron law of oligarchy.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: T.H. Marshall
facts.summary: British sociologist who traced the growth of citizenship from civil to political to social rights.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Thomas Robert Malthus
facts.summary: English clergyman and economist who argued that population tends to grow faster than the means of subsistence.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: William F. Ogburn
facts.summary: American sociologist who studied technology and social change and introduced the idea of cultural lag.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Andre Gunder Frank
facts.summary: German-born economic historian and sociologist of dependency theory who argued that capitalism produced Latin American underdevelopment.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Harry Braverman
facts.summary: American Marxist writer who argued that monopoly capitalism degrades work by deskilling it.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: G.S. Ghurye
facts.summary: Pioneer of Indian sociology at Bombay University who studied caste, tribes and Indian culture through an Indological approach.
facts.note: IGNOU Sociology Papers 1 and 2 give 1893-1984.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 1; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: M.N. Srinivas
facts.summary: Indian sociologist of the structural-functional and field-view approach who introduced Sanskritisation, Westernisation and dominant caste.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: A.R. Desai
facts.summary: Indian Marxist sociologist who analysed nationalism, peasant struggles and the post-colonial state in class terms.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Louis Dumont
facts.summary: French anthropologist who explained caste as a hierarchy grounded in the religious opposition of pure and impure.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: André Béteille
facts.summary: Indian sociologist who studied caste, class and power in a Tanjore village and the growing separation of these dimensions of inequality.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Yogendra Singh
facts.summary: Indian sociologist who analysed the modernisation of Indian tradition as cultural and structural, orthogenetic and heterogenetic change.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Irawati Karve
facts.summary: Indian anthropologist who mapped kinship organisation in India into regional zones.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: S.C. Dube
facts.summary: Indian anthropologist whose study of Shamirpet near Hyderabad was among the first Indian village monographs.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Robert Redfield
facts.summary: American anthropologist of peasant society who distinguished the great tradition and the little tradition of a civilisation.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: McKim Marriott
facts.summary: American anthropologist whose study of Kishan Garhi village described universalisation and parochialisation.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Milton Singer
facts.summary: American anthropologist who studied how Madras industrial leaders kept up Hindu tradition alongside modern industrial work.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Daniel Thorner
facts.summary: American economic historian of India who classified agrarian classes as malik, kisan and mazdur.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Verrier Elwin
facts.summary: British-born anthropologist of central Indian tribes who urged their protection from outside exploitation and later advised Nehru on tribal policy.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: N.K. Bose
facts.summary: Indian anthropologist who described how tribes were absorbed into Hindu society as castes.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: B.R. Ambedkar
facts.summary: Dalit leader, jurist and chair of the Constitution's Drafting Committee, who argued for the annihilation of caste.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 1; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Rajni Kothari
facts.summary: Indian political scientist who analysed the Congress system of one-party dominance and the politicisation of caste.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: A.M. Shah
facts.summary: Indian sociologist who studied the household as a dimension of the family in India.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844
facts.summary: Marx's early writings on the alienation of the worker from the product, the labour process, species-being and other people.
facts.note: Written in 1844; first published in full in 1932.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Communist Manifesto
facts.summary: Pamphlet declaring that the history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles.
facts.note: Co-written with Engels.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Capital, Volume I
facts.summary: Marx's analysis of capitalist production, showing how capital extracts surplus value from wage labour.
facts.note: Volumes II (1885) and III (1894) were edited by Engels and published after Marx's death.
facts.verified: books: Haralambos & Holborn; IGNOU Sociology Paper 1

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State
facts.summary: Links the rise of the monogamous family and the state to private property, drawing on Lewis Henry Morgan's Ancient Society.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Division of Labour in Society
aliases: The Division of Labor in Society
De la division du travail social
facts.summary: Argues that society moves from mechanical solidarity based on likeness to organic solidarity based on specialised interdependence.
facts.verified: books: Anthony Giddens; IGNOU Sociology Paper 1

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Rules of Sociological Method
facts.summary: Durkheim's statement of method: treat social facts as things and explain them by other social facts.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Suicide
facts.summary: Uses suicide rates to show how integration and regulation shape suicide, distinguishing egoistic, altruistic, anomic and fatalistic types.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Elementary Forms of the Religious Life
aliases: The Elementary Forms of Religious Life
facts.summary: Studies Australian Aboriginal totemism to argue that religion separates sacred from profane and that its real object is society itself.
facts.verified: books: Haralambos & Holborn; IGNOU Sociology Paper 1

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism
aliases: Die protestantische Ethik und der Geist des Kapitalismus
facts.summary: Argues that Calvinist ideas of calling and predestination fostered the disciplined, rational conduct suited to modern capitalism.
facts.note: Published as two essays in 1904-05 and revised in 1920; Talcott Parsons' English translation appeared in 1930.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Economy and Society
facts.summary: Weber's unfinished treatise on social action, legitimate authority, bureaucracy, and class, status and party.
facts.note: Published after his death by Marianne Weber in 1921-22; full English edition 1968.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Religion of India
aliases: The Religion of India: The Sociology of Hinduism and Buddhism
facts.summary: Weber's study of Hinduism and Buddhism, arguing that caste and the doctrines of karma and dharma did not favour a rational capitalist ethic.
facts.note: German essays 1916-17; English translation 1958.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Structure of Social Action
facts.summary: Draws on Marshall, Pareto, Durkheim and Weber to build a voluntaristic theory of action.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Social System
facts.summary: Treats society as a system of interrelated parts held together by shared values, institutionalised roles and socialisation.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Social Theory and Social Structure
facts.summary: Merton's collection on functional analysis, middle-range theory, reference groups and deviance.
facts.note: Enlarged editions appeared in 1957 and 1968.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Social Structure and Anomie
facts.summary: Article arguing that deviance arises when a culture stresses success goals but the social structure limits the legitimate means to reach them.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Mind, Self and Society
facts.summary: Lectures on how mind and self arise in social interaction through language, role-taking and the generalised other.
facts.note: Published after Mead's death from students' notes, edited by Charles W. Morris.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life
facts.summary: Analyses everyday interaction as a performance with front and back regions and impression management.
facts.note: First published in 1956 in Edinburgh; the widely cited US edition is 1959.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Sociological Imagination
facts.summary: Calls for a sociology that links personal troubles to public issues of social structure and history.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Power Elite
facts.summary: Argues that interlocking corporate, military and political elites hold power in the United States.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Some Principles of Stratification
facts.summary: Argues that stratification is functionally necessary, as unequal rewards draw the ablest people into the most important positions.
facts.note: Co-written with Wilbert E. Moore; criticised by Melvin Tumin in 1953.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: An Essay on the Principle of Population
aliases: Essay on the Principle of Population
facts.summary: Argues that population grows geometrically while subsistence grows arithmetically, so positive and preventive checks hold population down.
facts.verified: books: Anthony Giddens; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Development of Underdevelopment
facts.summary: Essay arguing that Latin American underdevelopment results from the satellite's exploitative ties to the capitalist metropolis.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Caste and Race in India
facts.summary: Ghurye's study of caste, setting out its six features and tracing it to Brahmanic Indo-Aryan culture in the Gangetic plain.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Aborigines—So-called—and Their Future
aliases: The Aborigines So-called and Their Future
facts.summary: Argues that Indian tribes are backward Hindus who should be integrated into Hindu society, not isolated.
facts.note: Later editions were titled The Scheduled Tribes.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Religion and Society among the Coorgs of South India
aliases: Religion and Society Among the Coorgs
facts.summary: Study of Coorg religion and ritual in which Srinivas introduced the concept of Sanskritisation.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Social Change in Modern India
facts.summary: Srinivas's lectures on Sanskritisation, Westernisation and secularisation as processes of change in Indian society.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Social Background of Indian Nationalism
aliases: The Social Background of Indian Nationalism
facts.summary: Marxist account of how British rule transformed India's economy and classes and so gave rise to Indian nationalism.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Homo Hierarchicus
aliases: Homo Hierarchicus: The Caste System and Its Implications
facts.summary: Argues that caste rests on hierarchy grounded in the opposition of pure and impure, with status encompassing power.
facts.note: French original 1966; IGNOU Paper 2 gives 1967 and IGNOU Paper 1 cites the 1972 Granada edition.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 1; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Caste, Class and Power
facts.summary: Study of Sripuram, a Tanjore village, showing caste, class and power growing apart as bases of stratification.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 2; Yogendra Singh

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Modernization of Indian Tradition
facts.summary: Analyses change in Indian society as orthogenetic and heterogenetic change in its cultural tradition and social structure.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Kinship Organisation in India
facts.summary: Karve's survey dividing Indian kinship into northern, central, southern and eastern zones.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 1; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Indian Village
facts.summary: Monograph on Shamirpet village near Hyderabad describing its caste, family, economy, ritual and change.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Peasant Society and Culture
facts.summary: Treats peasant society as a part-society linked to a wider civilisation through its great and little traditions.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: When a Great Tradition Modernizes
facts.summary: Study of Madras showing industrial leaders adapting Hindu tradition to modern industry rather than abandoning it.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Agrarian Prospect in India
facts.summary: Thorner's lectures on India's agrarian structure, dividing rural classes into malik, kisan and mazdur.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Annihilation of Caste
facts.summary: Argues that caste cannot be reformed and must be destroyed by rejecting the religious scriptures that sanction it.
facts.note: Written as a speech for the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal of Lahore, which cancelled the event; Ambedkar published it himself.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The Household Dimension of the Family in India
facts.summary: Argues that the household must be studied apart from the wider family and traces how Indian households change over time.
facts.note: Editions dated 1973 and 1974 are both cited.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Positivism
facts.summary: The view that society should be studied, like nature, through observation, comparison and experiment to discover its laws.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Law of three stages
facts.summary: Comte's law that human thought, and society with it, passes through theological, metaphysical and positive stages.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Historical materialism
facts.summary: Marx's view that the mode of production, combining forces and relations of production, shapes society and drives historical change.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Base and superstructure
facts.summary: Marx's model in which the economic base of production relations conditions the legal, political and ideological superstructure.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Alienation
facts.summary: Under capitalism the worker is estranged from the product, the act of production, human species-being and other people.
facts.verified: books: Haralambos & Holborn; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Class struggle
facts.summary: Conflict between classes defined by ownership of the means of production; a class-in-itself becomes a class-for-itself through shared consciousness.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Surplus value
facts.summary: The value workers create beyond the value of their wages, taken by the capitalist as the source of profit.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: False consciousness
facts.summary: Beliefs that hide real class relations and exploitation from those who are subordinated.
facts.note: The phrase is Engels's, from his 1893 letter to Franz Mehring; Marx never used it, though it is often credited to him.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Social fact
facts.summary: Ways of acting, thinking and feeling that are external to individuals and exercise constraint over them; to be treated as things.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Mechanical and organic solidarity
facts.summary: Mechanical solidarity binds similar people through a strong collective conscience; organic solidarity binds specialised, interdependent people through the division of labour.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Collective conscience
facts.summary: The totality of beliefs and sentiments common to average members of a society, forming a system with a life of its own.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Anomie
facts.summary: A state of deregulation in which social norms fail to limit individual desires, seen in anomic suicide and the anomic division of labour.
facts.note: Durkheim's concept; Merton later recast it as a gap between cultural goals and legitimate means.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Sacred and profane
facts.summary: Durkheim's division of things into the sacred, set apart and forbidden, and the profane; religion unites believers around sacred things.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 1; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Verstehen
facts.summary: Weber's method of understanding social action by grasping the subjective meanings actors attach to it.
facts.verified: books: Haralambos & Holborn; IGNOU Sociology Paper 1

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Ideal type
facts.summary: An analytical construct that one-sidedly accentuates features of reality, used to compare actual cases; neither a moral ideal nor an average.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Social action
facts.summary: Action oriented to the behaviour of others; Weber's four types are instrumentally rational, value-rational, affectual and traditional action.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Types of authority
facts.summary: Weber's three bases of legitimate domination: traditional, charismatic and legal-rational authority.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Bureaucracy
facts.summary: Weber's ideal type of legal-rational administration: hierarchy, written rules, impersonality, specialised trained officials and salaried careers.
facts.verified: books: Haralambos & Holborn; IGNOU Sociology Paper 1

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Rationalisation
facts.summary: The spread of calculable, rule-governed and efficient action in modern life, which brings the disenchantment of the world.
facts.note: The phrase 'iron cage' is Parsons' 1930 translation of Weber's 'stahlhartes Gehäuse'.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Value neutrality
facts.summary: Weber's principle that values may guide the choice of topic but personal value judgements must be kept out of scientific analysis.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Class, status and party
facts.summary: Weber's three dimensions of the distribution of power: class (market situation), status (social honour and lifestyle) and party (political organisation).

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: AGIL scheme
facts.summary: Parsons' four problems every social system must solve: adaptation, goal attainment, integration and latency, or pattern maintenance.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Pattern variables
facts.summary: Five pairs of choices that orient action, such as affectivity versus affective neutrality and universalism versus particularism.
facts.verified: books: Haralambos & Holborn; IGNOU Sociology Paper 1

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Manifest and latent functions
facts.summary: Manifest functions are intended and recognised consequences of a social item; latent functions are neither intended nor recognised.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Dysfunction
facts.summary: Merton's term for consequences of a social item that lessen the adaptation or adjustment of a system.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Theories of the middle range
facts.summary: Merton's call for theories between minor working hypotheses and all-inclusive grand theory, closely tied to empirical research.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Reference group
facts.summary: A group whose standards people use to judge themselves, including non-membership groups that lead to anticipatory socialisation.
facts.note: Herbert Hyman coined the term in 1942; Merton developed reference group theory.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 1; Yogendra Singh

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Relative deprivation
facts.summary: A sense of deprivation that comes from comparison with a reference group rather than from absolute conditions.
facts.note: The concept comes from Stouffer's The American Soldier (1949); Merton and Kitt developed it.
facts.verified: books: Anthony Giddens; IGNOU Sociology Paper 1

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Strain theory
facts.summary: Deviance arises when culture stresses success goals but limits legitimate means; adaptations are conformity, innovation, ritualism, retreatism and rebellion.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Self-fulfilling prophecy
facts.summary: A false definition of a situation that evokes new behaviour which makes the originally false conception come true.
facts.note: Merton coined the term in 1948, building on the Thomas theorem.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: The self (I and me)
facts.summary: Mead's self arises in social interaction; the 'I' is its spontaneous response and the 'me' the attitudes of others it has taken in.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Generalised other
facts.summary: The organised attitudes of the whole community, which a person takes into account in the game stage.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Looking-glass self
facts.summary: Cooley's idea that the self grows from imagining how we appear to others, how they judge us, and the feeling that results.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Symbolic interactionism
facts.summary: Perspective holding that people act on meanings that arise in social interaction and are handled through interpretation.
facts.note: Blumer coined the term in 1937; the ideas are largely Mead's, but Mead did not use it.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Dramaturgy
facts.summary: Goffman's view of interaction as a performance in which people manage the impressions they give to others.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Participant observation
facts.summary: Fieldwork method in which the researcher lives among the people studied and takes part in their daily life.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 1; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Alliance theory
facts.summary: Lévi-Strauss's theory that kinship rests on marriage alliances between groups, created by the exchange of women under the incest taboo.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Universality of the nuclear family
facts.summary: Murdock's claim that the nuclear family is universal and performs sexual, economic, reproductive and educational functions.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Vertical and horizontal mobility
facts.summary: Sorokin's distinction between movement up or down the social hierarchy and movement between positions at the same level.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 1; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Circulation of elites
facts.summary: Pareto's theory that history is a succession of elites, with lion-like and fox-like elites replacing one another.
facts.verified: books: Haralambos & Holborn; IGNOU Sociology Paper 1

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Iron law of oligarchy
facts.summary: Michels's law that every large organisation, even a democratic party, comes to be ruled by a small leadership.
facts.note: Set out in Political Parties: German original 1911, English translation 1915.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Citizenship rights
facts.summary: Marshall's account of citizenship in Britain expanding from civil rights to political rights and then to social rights.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Cultural lag
facts.summary: Ogburn's idea that non-material culture adapts more slowly than material culture and technology, creating strain.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Dependency theory
facts.summary: The view that poor countries are underdeveloped because of their exploitative dependence on the developed capitalist core.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Deskilling
facts.summary: Braverman's thesis, in Labor and Monopoly Capital, that monopoly capitalism separates conception from execution and strips workers of skill.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Ghurye's six features of caste
facts.summary: Segmental division, hierarchy, restrictions on feeding and social intercourse, civil and religious disabilities, restricted choice of occupation, and endogamy.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 1; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Sanskritisation
facts.summary: Process by which a low caste or tribe adopts the customs, rituals and way of life of a higher, often twice-born, caste to claim higher status.
facts.note: Introduced in the Coorgs study (1952); Srinivas first called it Brahminisation.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Westernisation
facts.summary: Srinivas's term for changes in Indian society and culture from over 150 years of British rule, in technology, institutions, ideology and values.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Dominant caste
facts.summary: A caste that dominates a village through numerical strength and economic and political power, helped by a ritual rank that is not too low.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 1; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Vote bank
facts.summary: A bloc of voters, often of one caste or community, delivered to a party through leaders who promise it benefits.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Purity and pollution
facts.summary: Dumont's principle that caste hierarchy rests on the opposition of pure and impure, placing the Brahmin at the top and the untouchable at the bottom.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 1; IGNOU Sociology Paper 2

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Great and little traditions
facts.summary: Redfield's distinction between the great tradition of the reflective few, carried in texts and temples, and the little tradition of the unreflective many in villages.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 2; Yogendra Singh

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Universalisation and parochialisation
facts.summary: Marriott's two processes: little-tradition elements rise into the great tradition, and great-tradition elements are taken into local practice.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Sociology Paper 2; Yogendra Singh

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Compartmentalisation
facts.summary: Singer's term for how Madras industrialists kept modern work and traditional ritual life in separate spheres.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Isolationist approach to tribes
facts.summary: Elwin's early proposal to protect tribal areas from outside contact and exploitation, often called the national park approach.
facts.note: Elwin later moved towards integration as adviser for NEFA.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Hindu method of tribal absorption
facts.summary: Bose's account of how tribes entered Hindu society as castes, drawn by the economic security of the caste division of labour.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Congress system
facts.summary: Kothari's term for the Congress-dominated party system, in which opposition parties worked as parties of pressure on its margins.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Jajmani system
facts.summary: Hereditary exchange in which service castes serve landowning patron families in return for grain and other customary payments.
facts.note: First analysed as a system in W.H. Wiser's The Hindu Jajmani System (1936).

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Demographic transition theory
facts.summary: Theory that populations move from high birth and death rates, through falling death rates, to low birth and death rates.
facts.note: Giddens credits Warren Thompson with the 1929 pattern; the geography books date Notestein's model to 1945.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Tribal Panchsheel
facts.summary: Nehru's five principles for tribal policy, stressing development along tribes' own genius, land and forest rights, and tribal self-administration.
facts.note: Set out in Nehru's foreword to Elwin's A Philosophy for NEFA; not the 1954 India-China Panchsheel.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: French Revolution
facts.summary: Overthrow of the French monarchy which, with the Industrial Revolution, raised the problems of order and change from which sociology emerged.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: First Census of India
facts.summary: The first all-India census, taken region by region at different times rather than on one date.
facts.note: Not synchronous; the first synchronous census was held in 1881.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Constitution of India comes into force
facts.summary: The Constitution came into force and India became a republic committed to justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
facts.note: Adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Community Development Programme
facts.summary: Programme of all-round rural development, launched in selected areas, to improve farming, health, education and welfare through people's participation.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Balwantrai Mehta Committee
facts.summary: Committee that reviewed the Community Development Programme and recommended three-tier Panchayati Raj as democratic decentralisation.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: National Family Planning Programme
facts.summary: India became the first country to start a national family planning programme.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Mandal Commission
facts.summary: Commission under B.P. Mandal that identified Other Backward Classes and recommended 27 per cent reservation for them.
facts.note: Set up in 1979, reported in 1980; the V.P. Singh government decided to implement it in 1990.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: 73rd Constitutional Amendment
facts.summary: Gave constitutional status to three-tier Panchayati Raj, with one-third of seats reserved for women and reservation for SCs and STs.
facts.note: Passed in 1992; came into force on 24 April 1993.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: Chipko movement
facts.summary: Villagers in the Garhwal Himalaya, many of them women, hugged trees to stop the commercial felling of their forests.

facts.subject: sociology
facts.name: National Population Policy 2000
facts.summary: Set replacement-level fertility as the medium-term goal and a stable population by 2045 as the long-term goal.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Edward Burnett Tylor
facts.summary: British classical evolutionist who gave the classic definition of culture and proposed animism as the earliest form of religion.
facts.note: Not Stephen Tyler, the cognitive anthropologist.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: James George Frazer
facts.summary: British classical evolutionist who traced a sequence from magic through religion to science.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Lewis Henry Morgan
facts.summary: American classical evolutionist who studied the Iroquois, founded kinship studies and set out stages of savagery, barbarism and civilisation.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: John Ferguson McLennan
facts.summary: Scottish evolutionist who coined exogamy and endogamy and argued that early marriage was by capture.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Franz Boas
facts.summary: German-born founder of American anthropology who rejected unilinear evolution and stressed each culture's particular history and cultural relativism.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Alfred Louis Kroeber
facts.summary: Boas's student who treated culture as superorganic and mapped the culture areas of native North America.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Clark Wissler
facts.summary: American diffusionist who developed the culture area and age-area concepts from American Indian data.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Ruth Benedict
facts.summary: Culture-and-personality pioneer who saw each culture as an integrated configuration, like a personality writ large.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Margaret Mead
facts.summary: Benedict's student whose Samoa and New Guinea studies argued that adolescence and sex roles are shaped by culture.
facts.note: Not George Herbert Mead, the sociologist.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Ralph Linton
facts.summary: American anthropologist who defined status and role and worked with Kardiner on basic personality structure.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Abram Kardiner
facts.summary: American psychoanalyst who, with Linton, held that primary institutions such as child-rearing form a society's basic personality structure.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Cora Du Bois
facts.summary: American anthropologist whose fieldwork on Alor in Indonesia produced the concept of modal personality.
facts.note: Not W.E.B. Du Bois.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Bronisław Malinowski
facts.summary: Polish-born British anthropologist who founded functionalism and modern participant-observation fieldwork in the Trobriand Islands.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: A.R. Radcliffe-Brown
facts.summary: British founder of structural-functionalism, who studied how institutions maintain social structure; did fieldwork in the Andaman Islands.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: E.E. Evans-Pritchard
facts.summary: British social anthropologist known for his studies of Azande witchcraft and the stateless, segmentary Nuer.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Edmund Leach
facts.summary: British anthropologist who showed Kachin politics swinging between gumsa and gumlao forms and brought structuralism into British anthropology.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Claude Lévi-Strauss
facts.summary: French founder of structural anthropology, who read kinship, myth and classification as products of universal binary structures of the mind.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Victor Turner
facts.summary: British symbolic anthropologist who studied Ndembu ritual and developed the ideas of liminality and communitas.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Arnold van Gennep
facts.summary: French ethnographer and folklorist who identified the three-phase structure of rites of passage.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Clifford Geertz
facts.summary: American interpretive anthropologist who treated culture as public webs of meaning to be read through thick description.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: David M. Schneider
facts.summary: American symbolic anthropologist who studied kinship as a cultural system of symbols and meanings.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Stephen A. Tyler
facts.summary: American cognitive anthropologist who edited Cognitive Anthropology (1969) and later wrote on post-modern ethnography.
facts.note: Not E.B. Tylor, the classical evolutionist.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Harold C. Conklin
facts.summary: American ethnoscientist who studied Hanunóo colour categories and swidden farming in the Philippines through the people's own classifications.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Mary Douglas
facts.summary: British anthropologist who treated pollution as a matter of classification, with dirt as matter out of place, and devised grid-group analysis.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Leslie A. White
facts.summary: American neo-evolutionist who tied cultural evolution to the energy harnessed per person (universal evolution).

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Julian Steward
facts.summary: American neo-evolutionist who proposed multilinear evolution and founded cultural ecology.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Marshall Sahlins
facts.summary: American anthropologist who, with Service, separated general and specific evolution, and classified reciprocity in Stone Age Economics.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Elman Service
facts.summary: American neo-evolutionist who classified political organisation into band, tribe, chiefdom and state.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: V. Gordon Childe
facts.summary: Australian-born prehistorian and neo-evolutionist who named the Neolithic and Urban Revolutions.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Marvin Harris
facts.summary: American founder of cultural materialism, which explains culture by its techno-economic and demographic infrastructure.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Karl Polanyi
facts.summary: Hungarian economic historian whose substantivist approach classed economies by reciprocity, redistribution and market exchange.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Marcel Mauss
facts.summary: French sociologist and Durkheim's nephew who analysed the gift as a total social fact binding giver and receiver.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Émile Durkheim
facts.summary: French sociologist who defined religion by the sacred and studied Australian totemism as its elementary form.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: R.R. Marett
facts.summary: British anthropologist who proposed animatism, belief in an impersonal supernatural power, as a stage before animism.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Max Müller
facts.summary: German-born Oxford philologist and Indologist who explained the origin of religion as naturism, the personification of nature.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Grafton Elliot Smith
facts.summary: Australian-born anatomist and British diffusionist who, with W.J. Perry, derived all civilisation from ancient Egypt.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: W.H.R. Rivers
facts.summary: British anthropologist and psychologist who devised the genealogical method, studied the Todas and later turned to diffusionism.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Edward Sapir
facts.summary: American linguist-anthropologist and student of Boas whose view that language shapes thought underlies the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Fredrik Barth
facts.summary: Norwegian anthropologist who defined ethnic groups by the boundaries they maintain rather than by their cultural content.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Charles Darwin
facts.summary: English naturalist who proposed evolution by natural selection.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Gregor Mendel
facts.summary: Augustinian friar of Brünn (Brno) whose pea-plant experiments gave the laws of segregation and independent assortment.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Thomas Robert Malthus
facts.summary: English economist who argued that population grows geometrically while food supply grows only arithmetically.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Herbert Hope Risley
facts.summary: British administrator and Census Commissioner for 1901 who classified India's people into seven racial types and gave a racial theory of caste.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: J.H. Hutton
facts.summary: British administrator-ethnographer of the Nagas and Census Commissioner for 1931, who wrote Caste in India.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Sarat Chandra Roy
facts.summary: Ranchi lawyer and pioneer Indian ethnographer of the Munda, Oraon and other Chotanagpur tribes, who founded the journal Man in India.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: B.S. Guha
facts.summary: Indian physical anthropologist who classified India's population into six main racial elements and was the first director of the Anthropological Survey of India.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Verrier Elwin
facts.summary: British-born ethnographer of central Indian tribes who first argued for shielding them from outsiders, then advised Nehru on tribal policy in NEFA.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: G.S. Ghurye
facts.summary: Indian sociologist who set out six features of caste and called tribes backward Hindus, arguing for their assimilation.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: D.N. Majumdar
facts.summary: Lucknow anthropologist who studied the Ho and other tribes, race and caste in India, and village communities.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Nirmal Kumar Bose
facts.summary: Indian anthropologist who described the Hindu method of tribal absorption and the structure of Hindu society.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Irawati Karve
facts.summary: Indian anthropologist who mapped Indian kinship into northern, central, southern and eastern zones.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: L.P. Vidyarthi
facts.summary: Ranchi anthropologist who formulated the sacred complex and the Nature-Man-Spirit complex and traced the phases of Indian anthropology.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: S.C. Dube
facts.summary: Indian anthropologist whose study of Shamirpet near Hyderabad was among the first full Indian village monographs.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: M.N. Srinivas
facts.summary: Indian social anthropologist who formulated Sanskritisation, Westernisation and dominant caste, and studied the village of Rampura.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Robert Redfield
facts.summary: American anthropologist of peasant society who proposed the folk-urban continuum and the great and little traditions.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: McKim Marriott
facts.summary: American anthropologist whose study of Kishan Garhi village described universalisation and parochialisation.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Louis Dumont
facts.summary: French anthropologist who explained caste as hierarchy built on the opposition of the pure and the impure.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: F.G. Bailey
facts.summary: British anthropologist of highland Odisha who proposed the tribe-caste continuum.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf
facts.summary: Austrian-born anthropologist of the tribes of Hyderabad and North-East India who advised on tribal welfare.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Primitive Culture
facts.summary: Opens with Tylor's definition of culture as a complex whole and sets out animism and survivals in an evolutionary account of religion.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The Golden Bough
aliases: The Golden Bough: A Study in Magic and Religion
facts.summary: Comparative study of magic and religion proposing an evolutionary sequence from magic to religion to science.
facts.note: First published in two volumes in 1890; later enlarged to twelve volumes.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Ancient Society
facts.summary: Traces human progress through savagery, barbarism and civilisation, linked to inventions, forms of family, government and property.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The Mind of Primitive Man
facts.summary: Argues that race, language and culture vary independently and that no race is innately inferior in mental capacity.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Patterns of Culture
facts.summary: Compares the Zuni, Dobu and Kwakiutl as integrated configurations, calling the Zuni Apollonian and the Kwakiutl Dionysian.
facts.note: Benedict took the Apollonian-Dionysian contrast from Nietzsche.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Coming of Age in Samoa
facts.summary: Argues that Samoan girls pass through adolescence without Western stress, so adolescent turmoil is cultural rather than biological.
facts.note: Challenged by Derek Freeman in 1983.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Argonauts of the Western Pacific
facts.summary: Trobriand ethnography of the Kula exchange that set the model for long-term participant-observation fieldwork.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Structure and Function in Primitive Society
facts.summary: Collected essays setting out structural-functionalism, including those on the mother's brother and on joking relationships.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Witchcraft, Oracles and Magic Among the Azande
facts.summary: Shows Azande witchcraft beliefs as a coherent system for explaining misfortune, separating inborn witchcraft from learned sorcery.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The Nuer
facts.summary: Describes the ecology and political institutions of the Nuer, a stateless people held together by a segmentary lineage system.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Political Systems of Highland Burma
facts.summary: Shows Kachin communities oscillating between hierarchical gumsa and egalitarian gumlao forms, challenging the idea of stable equilibrium.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The Elementary Structures of Kinship
aliases: Les Structures élémentaires de la parenté
facts.summary: Founds alliance theory: the incest taboo forces groups to exchange women, through restricted or generalised exchange.
facts.note: French original 1949; English translation 1969.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The Ritual Process
aliases: The Ritual Process: Structure and Anti-Structure
facts.summary: Uses Ndembu ritual to develop liminality and communitas, the bond among equals in the in-between phase of ritual.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Les Rites de Passage
facts.summary: Shows that ceremonies of life crises and transitions share three phases: separation, transition and incorporation.
facts.note: French original 1909; English translation 1960.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The Interpretation of Cultures
facts.summary: Essays presenting culture as webs of meaning read through thick description, including 'Religion as a Cultural System'.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: American Kinship: A Cultural Account
facts.summary: Analyses American kinship as a system of symbols resting on shared biogenetic substance and a code for conduct.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Anthropology Paper 1; IGNOU Anthropology Paper 2

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Purity and Danger
facts.summary: Argues that ideas of pollution and taboo protect a society's system of classification; dirt is matter out of place.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Stone Age Economics
facts.summary: Calls hunter-gatherers the original affluent society and classifies reciprocity as generalised, balanced or negative.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Man Makes Himself
facts.summary: Presents prehistory as a series of revolutions, chiefly the Neolithic and Urban Revolutions, driven by technology and economy.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The Gift
aliases: The Gift: Forms and Functions of Exchange in Archaic Societies
facts.summary: Argues that gifts in archaic societies carry obligations to give, to receive and to repay, forming total social facts.
facts.note: French original 1925 (some books give 1924); English translation 1954.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The Elementary Forms of Religious Life
aliases: The Elementary Forms of the Religious Life
Les Formes élémentaires de la vie religieuse
facts.summary: Defines religion by the division of sacred and profane and studies Australian totemism as its elementary form.
facts.note: French original 1912; English translation 1915.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The Todas
facts.summary: Ethnography of the Todas of the Nilgiris, known for fraternal polyandry and buffalo dairy ritual, built on recorded genealogies.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Ethnic Groups and Boundaries
facts.summary: Edited volume whose introduction argues that ethnic groups persist through boundaries kept up in interaction, not shared culture alone.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: On the Origin of Species
facts.summary: Sets out evolution by natural selection acting on heritable variation in the struggle for existence.
facts.note: Alfred Russel Wallace reached the same idea independently; their joint papers were read in 1858.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Anthropology Paper 1; Majumdar & Madan

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Experiments on Plant Hybridization
facts.summary: Reports pea-plant crosses showing that hereditary factors segregate and assort independently in fixed ratios.
facts.note: Read in 1865 and published in 1866; rediscovered in 1900 by de Vries, Correns and Tschermak.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: An Essay on the Principle of Population
aliases: Essay on the Principle of Population
facts.summary: Argues that population outruns food supply unless held back by positive checks such as famine and disease or by preventive checks.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The People of India
facts.summary: Classifies India's population into seven racial types from anthropometry and links caste rank to race.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Caste in India
facts.summary: Survey of the caste system that explains its origin partly through tribal ideas of mana and taboo.
facts.note: Not Ghurye's Caste and Race in India (1932).

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The Mundas and Their Country
facts.summary: Ethnography of the Munda of Chotanagpur, covering their history, land system and social life.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: A Philosophy for NEFA
facts.summary: Sets out a policy for developing the tribes of NEFA along the lines of their own culture, avoiding both isolation and forced assimilation.
facts.note: The 1959 second edition carries Nehru's foreword with the Tribal Panchsheel.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Caste and Race in India
facts.summary: Sets out six features of caste and traces its origin to the Brahmins of the Indo-Gangetic plain.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: The Sacred Complex in Hindu Gaya
facts.summary: Study of the pilgrimage town of Gaya that introduces the sacred complex of sacred geography, performances and specialists.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Indian Village
facts.summary: Monograph on Shamirpet near Hyderabad describing the village as a social system of castes, economy and ritual.
facts.note: Not Village India (1955), edited by McKim Marriott.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Religion and Society Among the Coorgs of South India
aliases: Religion and Society Among the Coorgs
facts.summary: Study of Coorg ritual and caste in which Srinivas first set out Sanskritisation.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Village India: Studies in the Little Community
facts.summary: Edited volume of Indian village studies, including Marriott's essay on universalisation and parochialisation in Kishan Garhi.
facts.note: Not S.C. Dube's Indian Village (1955).

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Peasant Society and Culture
facts.summary: Describes peasant culture as a little tradition linked to the great tradition of a wider civilisation.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Homo Hierarchicus
aliases: Homo Hierarchicus: The Caste System and Its Implications
facts.summary: Explains the caste system as hierarchy based on the opposition of pure and impure, in which status encompasses power.
facts.note: French original 1966; English translation 1970.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Tribe, Caste and Nation
facts.summary: Study of political activity and change among the Konds and Oriyas of highland Odisha.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Kinship Organisation in India
facts.summary: Compares kinship terms and marriage rules across India and divides them into northern, central, southern and eastern zones.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Tribes of India: The Struggle for Survival
facts.summary: Surveys how land alienation, forest policy and development have pressed on India's tribes since independence.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Animism
facts.summary: Tylor's theory that religion began as belief in spiritual beings, an idea drawn from dreams, trances and death.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Animatism
facts.summary: Marett's term for belief in an impersonal supernatural power, such as mana, which he placed before animism.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Naturism
facts.summary: Max Müller's theory that religion arose from awe of the forces of nature, personified through language as gods.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Mana
facts.summary: Melanesian and Polynesian idea of an impersonal supernatural power that can reside in people and things.
facts.note: Reported by R.H. Codrington in The Melanesians (1891); Marett built animatism on it.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Sympathetic magic
facts.summary: Frazer's two kinds of magic: homeopathic, based on the law of similarity, and contagious, based on the law of contact.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Sacred and profane
facts.summary: Durkheim's division of things into the sacred, set apart and forbidden, and the ordinary profane; religion unites believers around the sacred.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Rites de passage
facts.summary: Ceremonies marking a change of status, passing through phases of separation, transition (liminal) and incorporation.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Liminality
facts.summary: The in-between phase of a rite of passage, where initiates are betwixt and between and share communitas.
facts.note: IGNOU Paper 1: introduced by Van Gennep (1909) and elaborated by Victor Turner and Edmund Leach; IGNOU Paper 2 credits Turner.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Anthropology Paper 1; IGNOU Anthropology Paper 2

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Revitalization movement
facts.summary: A deliberate, organised effort by members of a society to build a more satisfying culture, as defined by Anthony F.C. Wallace.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Kula ring
facts.summary: Trobriand ceremonial exchange in which shell necklaces (soulava) travel clockwise and armshells (mwali) anticlockwise between island partners.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Substantivism
facts.summary: Polanyi's view that pre-market economies are embedded in social relations and run by reciprocity and redistribution; formalists apply market economics everywhere.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Band, tribe, chiefdom and state
facts.summary: Service's evolutionary typology of political organisation by increasing scale, centralisation and inequality.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Exogamy and endogamy
facts.summary: Rules requiring marriage outside one's own group (exogamy) or within it (endogamy); McLennan coined both terms in Primitive Marriage.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Classificatory kinship terminology
facts.summary: Morgan's contrast between terms that group lineal and collateral kin under one word (classificatory) and terms that keep them apart (descriptive).

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Alliance theory
facts.summary: Treats kinship as built on marriage exchange between groups rather than on descent, against the descent theory of Radcliffe-Brown and Fortes.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Structuralism
facts.summary: Lévi-Strauss's search for the universal, unconscious structures of the mind, often binary oppositions, beneath kinship, myth and classification.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Historical particularism
facts.summary: Boas's approach that each culture is the product of its own particular history, to be studied in detail before any generalisation.
facts.note: The name was given by Marvin Harris in 1968, not by Boas.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Cultural relativism
facts.summary: The principle that a culture's beliefs and practices should be understood in its own terms, not judged by another culture's standards.
facts.note: Rooted in Boas; the term and its fullest statement came later, notably from Melville Herskovits.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Superorganic
facts.summary: Kroeber's view that culture is a level of reality above the individual and the organic, following its own patterns.
facts.note: Herbert Spencer used the word earlier; Kroeber's 1917 essay gave it its anthropological sense.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Culture area
facts.summary: A geographical region whose peoples share a common set of culture traits, spreading from a culture centre.
facts.note: Otis T. Mason used the term first; Wissler developed it and Kroeber refined it.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Status and role
facts.summary: Linton's distinction of status as a position in a social system and role as its behavioural side; status is either ascribed or achieved.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Basic personality structure
facts.summary: Personality traits shared by a society's members, shaped by primary institutions such as child-rearing and projected into secondary institutions such as religion.
facts.note: Developed jointly by Kardiner and Ralph Linton.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Modal personality
facts.summary: The personality type found most often in a society, measured statistically, as Cora Du Bois found on Alor.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Functionalism
facts.summary: Malinowski's theory that every element of culture works to satisfy basic biological needs and the derived needs they create.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Structural-functionalism
facts.summary: Radcliffe-Brown's theory that institutions function to maintain the social structure, the network of relations between persons.
facts.note: Radcliffe-Brown rejected Malinowski's needs-based functionalism.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Thick description
facts.summary: Geertz's method of describing behaviour together with the layered meanings it carries for the people involved.
facts.note: Geertz took the term from the philosopher Gilbert Ryle.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: White's law of cultural evolution
facts.summary: Culture evolves as the energy harnessed per person per year increases, or as the efficiency of the tools using it increases (C = E x T).

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Multilinear evolution
facts.summary: Steward's view that cultures in similar environments follow parallel paths of development, rather than one universal sequence.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Cultural ecology
facts.summary: Steward's study of how a culture core of subsistence and economic arrangements adapts to its environment.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Neolithic Revolution
facts.summary: Childe's term for the shift from food gathering to food production by farming and herding, leading to settled village life.
facts.note: Childe paired it with the later Urban Revolution.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Cultural materialism
facts.summary: Harris's research strategy that explains structure and superstructure by the infrastructure of production and reproduction.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Heliocentric theory
facts.summary: British diffusionist view that civilisation arose once, in ancient Egypt, and spread across the world with sun-worshipping 'Children of the Sun'.
facts.note: Developed with W.J. Perry.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Kulturkreis
facts.summary: German-Austrian diffusionist theory that culture spread in complexes (culture circles) from a few centres, traced by criteria of form and quantity.
facts.note: Term from Leo Frobenius; method set out by Fritz Graebner and extended by Wilhelm Schmidt.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Genealogical method
facts.summary: Rivers's method of collecting full genealogies to trace kinship terms, marriage, descent and other social facts.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Emic and etic
facts.summary: Emic accounts describe a culture in its members' own categories; etic accounts use the observer's external, comparative categories.
facts.note: Coined by linguist Kenneth Pike from phonemic and phonetic; popularised by Marvin Harris.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Sapir-Whorf hypothesis
facts.summary: The idea that the structure of a language shapes how its speakers perceive and think about the world.
facts.note: Named after Sapir and his student Benjamin Lee Whorf; they never stated it jointly.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Hardy-Weinberg law
facts.summary: In a large, randomly mating population free of mutation, migration, selection and drift, allele and genotype frequencies stay constant.
facts.note: Stated independently by G.H. Hardy and Wilhelm Weinberg in 1908.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Anthropology Paper 1; P. Nath

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Synthetic theory of evolution
facts.summary: Joins Darwinian selection with Mendelian and population genetics: evolution results from mutation, recombination, selection, drift and isolation.
facts.note: Built by Dobzhansky, Mayr, Simpson, Julian Huxley and others.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Ramapithecus
facts.summary: Miocene ape from the Siwalik hills once claimed as an early human ancestor; now grouped with Sivapithecus as a relative of the orangutan.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Great tradition and little tradition
facts.summary: Redfield's contrast between the reflective, written culture of a civilisation's elite and the oral, local culture of village folk.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Universalisation and parochialisation
facts.summary: Universalisation carries little-tradition elements up into the great tradition; parochialisation carries great-tradition elements down into local forms.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Sanskritisation
facts.summary: The process by which a low caste or tribe adopts the customs, rituals and beliefs of a higher, often twice-born, caste to claim higher rank.
facts.note: Srinivas first called it Brahminisation in his Coorg study.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Dominant caste
facts.summary: A caste that holds numerical strength, economic and political power, and fairly high ritual rank in a village or region.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Westernisation
facts.summary: Srinivas's term for the changes in Indian society and culture that came with British rule, in technology, institutions, ideology and values.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Tribe-caste continuum
facts.summary: The view that tribe and caste are poles of one continuum, on which a group is placed by how directly its members hold land.
facts.note: Surajit Sinha also developed the idea.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Hindu method of tribal absorption
facts.summary: N.K. Bose's account of how tribes are drawn into Hindu society as castes while keeping many of their own customs.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Sacred complex
facts.summary: Vidyarthi's framework for a pilgrimage centre as the union of sacred geography, sacred performances and sacred specialists.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Nature-Man-Spirit complex
facts.summary: Vidyarthi's view, from his study of the Maler hill tribe, that nature, man and the spirit world form one interdependent whole.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Isolation policy
facts.summary: Elwin's early proposal to shield tribes from outside exploitation in protected areas, criticised as keeping them in 'national parks'.
facts.note: Elwin later moved towards integration in his NEFA work.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Tribal Panchsheel
facts.summary: Nehru's five principles for tribal policy: growth on their own genius, respect for land and forest rights, own people trained, no over-administration, results judged by human character.
facts.note: Set out in Nehru's foreword to Elwin's A Philosophy for NEFA.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Jajmani system
facts.summary: Hereditary patron-client ties in which service castes serve landowning patrons (jajmans) for fixed shares of grain and other dues.
facts.note: First described in detail by William Wiser in The Hindu Jajmani System (1936).

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
facts.summary: Tribal groups marked by pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness and a stagnant or declining population; 75 are listed.
facts.note: Called Primitive Tribal Groups until renamed in 2006.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Founding of the Asiatic Society
facts.summary: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in Calcutta, beginning systematic study of India's peoples, languages and antiquities.
facts.note: IGNOU and Xaxa give 1784 (Sir William Jones); Hasnain, citing Vidyarthi, prints 1774.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Anthropology Paper 1; Nadeem Hasnain; Xaxa

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Discovery of the Pallavaram handaxe
facts.summary: Robert Bruce Foote found a Palaeolithic handaxe at Pallavaram near Madras, the first recognised Palaeolithic tool in India.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Excavation of Harappa
facts.summary: Daya Ram Sahni began excavating Harappa, bringing the Indus (Harappan) Civilisation to light; R.D. Banerji found Mohenjo-daro soon after.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: First Census of India
facts.summary: The first census of British India, taken at different times in different regions, is dated 1872.
facts.note: The first synchronous census was held in 1881.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Founding of the Anthropological Survey of India
facts.summary: The Government of India set up the Anthropological Survey of India, with B.S. Guha as its first director.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: UNESCO Statement on Race
facts.summary: UNESCO's first statement on race declared humankind one species and proposed 'ethnic groups' in place of 'race' for human groups.
facts.note: Ashley Montagu was its rapporteur; revised statements followed.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Discovery of the Neanderthal type specimen
facts.summary: Quarrymen found the type fossil of Neanderthal man in the Feldhofer cave in the Neander valley near Düsseldorf, Germany.
facts.note: Earlier finds at Engis (1829) and Gibraltar (1848) were recognised as Neanderthal only later.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Discovery of Java Man
facts.summary: Eugène Dubois found a skullcap at Trinil on the Solo river in Java, the first fossil now classed as Homo erectus.
facts.note: Dubois named it Pithecanthropus erectus in 1894.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Discovery of Lucy
facts.summary: Donald Johanson's team found the partial skeleton of a female Australopithecus afarensis at Hadar in Ethiopia.
facts.note: The species Australopithecus afarensis was named in 1978.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Discovery of Narmada Man
facts.summary: Arun Sonakia of the Geological Survey of India found a hominin skull cap at Hathnora in the Narmada valley, the first hominin fossil from India.
facts.note: Sonakia classed it as Homo erectus; later studies treat it as archaic Homo sapiens.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Dhebar Commission
aliases: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes Commission
facts.summary: Commission under U.N. Dhebar that reviewed Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes and found wide inequality among tribes.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Anthropology Paper 2; Nadeem Hasnain

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Lokur Committee
facts.summary: Committee that set five criteria for listing Scheduled Tribes: primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Mandal Commission
facts.summary: Commission under B.P. Mandal that identified Other Backward Classes and recommended 27 per cent reservation for them in central government jobs.
facts.note: IGNOU Paper 2: constituted in 1978 under B.P. Mandal; Hasnain's table gives 1 January 1979; the report is of 1980.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act
facts.summary: Extends Panchayati Raj to Fifth Schedule areas and gives gram sabhas powers over land, minor forest produce and local resources.
facts.note: Based on the Bhuria Committee's recommendations.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Forest Rights Act
aliases: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act
facts.summary: Recognises individual and community rights of Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers over forest land and resources.
facts.note: Passed in 2006; in force from 31 December 2007.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Xaxa Committee
aliases: High Level Committee on tribal communities
facts.summary: High-level committee under Virginius Xaxa that reported on the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities.
facts.note: Set up in 2013; reported in 2014.

facts.subject: anthropology
facts.name: Santhal rebellion
facts.summary: Rising of the Santhals of the Rajmahal hills under Sidhu and Kanhu against zamindars, moneylenders and colonial officials.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Plato
facts.summary: Athenian philosopher whose Republic defines justice as each class doing its own work in a state ruled by philosopher-kings.
facts.note: Birth is given as 428 or 427 BCE, death as 348 or 347 BCE.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Aristotle
facts.summary: Greek philosopher, Plato's pupil, who called man a political animal by nature and classified constitutions.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; IGNOU Political Science Paper 2

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Kautilya
facts.summary: Ancient Indian theorist of statecraft credited with the Arthashastra, the saptanga theory of the state and the mandala theory of interstate relations.
facts.note: Dates are uncertain; tradition makes him the minister of Chandragupta Maurya, 4th century BCE.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Niccolò Machiavelli
facts.summary: Florentine thinker who separated politics from conventional morality and advised rulers how to gain and keep power.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Jean Bodin
facts.summary: French jurist who gave the first systematic theory of sovereignty as the absolute and perpetual power of a commonwealth.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Thomas Hobbes
facts.summary: English philosopher who argued that people escape a war-like state of nature by a social contract that creates an absolute sovereign.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: John Locke
facts.summary: English liberal who held that government rests on consent and exists to protect natural rights to life, liberty and property.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
facts.summary: Genevan philosopher who based legitimate authority on the general will of the sovereign people.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 2; O.P. Gauba

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: John Stuart Mill
facts.summary: English liberal who defended individual liberty, representative government and the equality of women.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Karl Marx
facts.summary: German thinker who explained history through class struggle and saw the state as an instrument of the ruling class.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Vladimir Lenin
facts.summary: Russian revolutionary who led the Bolshevik revolution of 1917 and explained imperialism as the highest stage of capitalism.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 2; O.P. Gauba

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Max Weber
facts.summary: German sociologist who defined the state by its monopoly of the legitimate use of physical force and classified types of legitimate authority.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Antonio Gramsci
facts.summary: Italian Marxist who explained class rule through hegemony, the consent won in civil society alongside coercion.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Harold Laski
facts.summary: British political theorist who argued for a pluralist state that shares sovereignty with other associations.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Hannah Arendt
facts.summary: German-American theorist of totalitarianism and of political action in a shared public realm, who separated power from violence.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Isaiah Berlin
facts.summary: British liberal philosopher who distinguished negative liberty from positive liberty and defended value pluralism.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Simone de Beauvoir
facts.summary: French existentialist feminist who argued that society makes woman man's Other.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: John Rawls
facts.summary: American philosopher whose theory of justice as fairness revived liberal political philosophy.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Robert Nozick
facts.summary: American libertarian who defended a minimal state and an entitlement theory of justice against Rawls.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Amartya Sen
facts.summary: Indian economist and philosopher who judges justice and development by people's real capabilities and freedoms.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Michael Walzer
facts.summary: American communitarian thinker who argues that each social good should be distributed by its own criteria.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Joseph Schumpeter
facts.summary: Austrian-American economist who redefined democracy as competition between leaders for the people's vote.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Robert Dahl
facts.summary: American political scientist of pluralism who called real-world democracies polyarchies.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Jürgen Habermas
facts.summary: German philosopher of the public sphere and communicative action, central to deliberative democracy.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: David Easton
facts.summary: Canadian-American political scientist who built systems analysis and led the post-behavioural revolution.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Gabriel Almond
facts.summary: American political scientist who developed the structural-functional approach and the study of political culture.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Steven Lukes
facts.summary: British theorist who argued that power has three dimensions, including the shaping of people's wants.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Ralph Miliband
facts.summary: British Marxist who saw the capitalist state as serving the ruling class, an instrumentalist view he debated with Poulantzas.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Hamza Alavi
facts.summary: Pakistani Marxist scholar who described the post-colonial state as overdeveloped and relatively autonomous of the propertied classes.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Friedrich Hayek
facts.summary: Austrian-British economist who argued that central planning destroys liberty and defended the free market and the rule of law.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Maurice Duverger
facts.summary: French political scientist who classified parties and party systems and linked electoral systems to the number of parties.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Rajni Kothari
facts.summary: Indian political scientist who described the Congress system of one-party dominance and the politicisation of caste.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Hans Morgenthau
facts.summary: German-American founder of classical realism, who saw international politics as a struggle for power.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: E. H. Carr
facts.summary: British historian whose attack on interwar utopianism opened the realist-idealist debate in international relations.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Kenneth Waltz
facts.summary: American founder of neorealism, who explained state behaviour by the anarchic structure of the international system.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: John Mearsheimer
facts.summary: American theorist of offensive realism, who holds that great powers maximise relative power and seek hegemony.

facts.subject: polsci
facts.name: Robert Keohane
