facts.summary: Osborne and Gaebler's model of government that steers rather than rows and is competitive, mission-driven, results-oriented and customer-driven.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: New Public Service
facts.summary: The Denhardts' alternative to NPM: government should serve citizens rather than customers and help them build a shared public interest.
facts.note: Article version 2000; book The New Public Service: Serving, Not Steering 2003.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Incrementalism
facts.summary: Lindblom's model in which policy changes in small steps from existing policy, agreed through partisan mutual adjustment among groups.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Optimal model
facts.summary: Dror's model joining rational analysis with extra-rational elements such as judgement and intuition, plus meta-policy-making and learning from feedback.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Mixed scanning
facts.summary: Etzioni's third approach to decisions: a broad scan of all options, then close study of a few, joining the rational and incremental models.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Multiple streams model
facts.summary: Kingdon's model: policy changes when separate problem, policy and politics streams meet in an open policy window, helped by policy entrepreneurs.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Garbage can model
facts.summary: Model of organisations as organised anarchies where problems, solutions, participants and choices mix, and decisions come when they meet by chance.
facts.note: Co-written by Michael Cohen, James March and Johan Olsen.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Rule of law
facts.summary: Dicey's three meanings: no punishment except for a breach of law proved in ordinary courts, equality of all before the law, and rights rooted in court decisions.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Delegated legislation
facts.summary: Rules made by the executive under powers given by an Act of the legislature; Lord Hewart attacked its growth in The New Despotism (1929).

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Ecological approach
facts.summary: Studies administration through its environment; Gaus listed factors such as people, place, technology, ideas, catastrophe and personality.
facts.note: Introduced by Gaus in Reflections on Public Administration (1947); developed by Riggs.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Development administration
facts.summary: Administration of planned programmes for economic growth and social change in developing countries, as distinct from routine law-and-order administration.
facts.note: Term credited to U.L. Goswami (1955); Weidner and Riggs developed the concept.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Anti-development thesis
facts.summary: Critique by Escobar, Sachs, Esteva and others that 'development' is a Western discourse that harms local cultures, livelihoods and the environment.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Soft state
facts.summary: Myrdal's term, from Asian Drama, for states that lack social discipline and fail to enforce their own laws and policies.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Good governance
facts.summary: Governance that is participatory, consensus-oriented, accountable, transparent, responsive, effective, equitable and inclusive, and follows the rule of law.
facts.note: Popularised by the World Bank from 1989; the eight features are the UN-ESCAP list.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Displacement of goals
facts.summary: Merton's bureaucratic dysfunction, from 'Bureaucratic Structure and Personality', in which following rules becomes an end in itself and displaces the real goals.
facts.note: Merton also used Thorstein Veblen's term 'trained incapacity'.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Contingency theory
facts.summary: No one best way to organise: the right structure depends on environment, technology and size; developed by Burns and Stalker, Woodward, and Lawrence and Lorsch.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Achievement motivation theory
facts.summary: McClelland's theory that people are driven by three learned needs: achievement, power and affiliation.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Expectancy theory
facts.summary: Motivation depends on expectancy (effort leads to performance), instrumentality (performance brings reward) and valence (how much the reward is valued).

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Fiedler's contingency model
facts.summary: Leader effectiveness depends on matching the leader's style, measured by the LPC scale, to how favourable the situation is.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Managerial Grid
facts.summary: Grid plotting concern for production against concern for people; team management (9,9) is the ideal style.
facts.note: Developed with Jane Mouton.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Representative bureaucracy
facts.summary: A civil service whose make-up mirrors the society it serves, which makes it more responsive to all groups.
facts.note: Term from J. Donald Kingsley's Representative Bureaucracy (1944).

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Steel frame
facts.summary: Name for the Indian Civil Service, and later the all-India services, as the frame that holds the administration together.
facts.note: Lloyd George used the phrase for the ICS in 1922; Patel defended the all-India services in 1949.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Planning-programming-budgeting system
facts.summary: Budget system linking objectives, programmes and costs over several years; it began in the US Defense Department under McNamara.
facts.note: Extended to all US federal agencies in 1965.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Zero-based budgeting
facts.summary: Every activity must be justified afresh each year as a ranked decision package, as if the budget started from zero.
facts.note: Developed by Peter Pyhrr at Texas Instruments; Jimmy Carter applied it in Georgia and then in the US federal government.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Performance budgeting
facts.summary: Budget classified by functions, programmes and activities, linking the money spent to the work done and its results.
facts.note: The term comes from the first Hoover Commission (1949).

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Programme Evaluation and Review Technique
facts.summary: Network technique for planning projects with optimistic, most likely and pessimistic time estimates; first used in the US Navy's Polaris missile programme.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Public Administration Paper 1; Mohit Bhattacharya

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Saptanga theory
facts.summary: Kautilya's seven elements of the state: swami (king), amatya (ministers), janapada, durga (fort), kosha (treasury), danda (army) and mitra (ally).

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Mansabdari system
facts.summary: Akbar's system of ranks (zat and sawar) that fixed each noble's status, pay and the number of cavalry he kept.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Indicative planning
facts.summary: Planning in which the state sets broad goals and guides the private sector through incentives, not fixed targets; India adopted it from the Eighth Plan (1992-97).

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Hawthorne studies
facts.summary: Studies at Western Electric's Hawthorne Works near Chicago which found that social factors and group norms shaped output; the basis of the human relations school.
facts.note: Mayo's Harvard team joined in 1927; many books date the studies 1927-32.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Minnowbrook Conference I
facts.summary: Conference of young scholars at Syracuse University's Minnowbrook centre, sponsored by Dwight Waldo, that launched New Public Administration.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Public Administration Paper 1; Mohit Bhattacharya

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Minnowbrook Conference II
facts.summary: Second Minnowbrook conference, held twenty years after the first to review public administration and the legacy of New Public Administration.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Public Administration Paper 1; Mohit Bhattacharya

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Minnowbrook Conference III
facts.summary: Third Minnowbrook conference, forty years after the first, on the future of public administration and governance in a global setting.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Northcote-Trevelyan Report
facts.summary: British report that called for civil service recruitment by open competitive examination and promotion on merit.
facts.note: Dated November 1853; published in 1854.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Public Administration Paper 2; Mohit Bhattacharya

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Macaulay Committee Report
facts.summary: Report on the Indian Civil Service recommending entry by open competitive examination; the first examination was held in London in 1855.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Fulton Committee Report
facts.summary: British report on the civil service that criticised the cult of the generalist and led to a Civil Service Department and a Civil Service College.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Citizen's Charter
facts.summary: UK programme under John Major that published service standards and means of redress; India adopted citizen's charters in 1997.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Ombudsman in Sweden
facts.summary: Sweden set up the first parliamentary Ombudsman to hear citizens' complaints against officials, the model for later ombudsman bodies such as the Lokpal.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Public Administration Paper 1; IGNOU Public Administration Paper 2

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Ripon's Resolution on Local Self-Government
facts.summary: Lord Ripon's resolution for elected local boards, which earned him the title 'father of local self-government in India'.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Office of the District Collector created
facts.summary: Warren Hastings created the post of Collector to run revenue collection in each district, the base of district administration.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Planning Commission
facts.summary: Set up by a Union Cabinet resolution, not by the Constitution or a statute, with the Prime Minister as its chairman.
facts.verified: books: Avasthi & Maheshwari; IGNOU Public Administration Paper 2

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: NITI Aayog
facts.summary: Replaced the Planning Commission as a policy think tank based on cooperative federalism.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Community Development Programme
facts.summary: Launched in 55 project areas to develop rural areas through people's participation, with the block as the unit of work.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Balwantrai Mehta Committee
facts.summary: Study team on the Community Development Programme that recommended three-tier Panchayati Raj; Rajasthan began it at Nagaur on 2 October 1959.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Ashok Mehta Committee
facts.summary: Committee on Panchayati Raj institutions that recommended a two-tier system of Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat.
facts.note: Appointed in 1977; reported in 1978.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act
facts.summary: Gave panchayats constitutional status: Part IX, three tiers, reserved seats, five-year terms, State Election and Finance Commissions, and the Eleventh Schedule.
facts.note: Passed in December 1992; in force from 24 April 1993.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act
facts.summary: Gave municipalities constitutional status: Part IXA, three types of municipality, the Twelfth Schedule, and district and metropolitan planning committees.
facts.note: Passed in December 1992; in force from 1 June 1993.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: First Administrative Reforms Commission
facts.summary: Chaired first by Morarji Desai and then K. Hanumanthaiya; gave 20 reports, the first urging a Lokpal and Lokayuktas.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Second Administrative Reforms Commission
facts.summary: Chaired first by Veerappa Moily and then V. Ramachandran; gave 15 reports, the first on the Right to Information.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Gorwala Report
facts.summary: A.D. Gorwala's report to the Planning Commission on making administration efficient and clean enough to carry out the plans.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Public Administration Paper 1; IGNOU Public Administration Paper 2

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Central Vigilance Commission
facts.summary: Set up by government resolution on the Santhanam Committee's advice to check corruption; made statutory by the CVC Act, 2003.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Public Administration Paper 2; Rumki Basu

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act
facts.summary: Set up a Lokpal at the Centre and required states to set up Lokayuktas to inquire into corruption by public servants.
facts.note: Passed in December 2013; assent on 1 January 2014.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Right to Information Act
facts.summary: Came fully into force, letting any citizen get information from public authorities, normally within 30 days.
facts.note: Assented to on 15 June 2005; fully in force from 12 October 2005.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Kothari Committee
facts.summary: Committee on recruitment policy whose three-stage examination (preliminary, main and interview) was used for the civil services from 1979.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Public Administration Paper 2; Mohit Bhattacharya

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: National Police Commission
facts.summary: Commission chaired by Dharma Vira that gave eight reports on police reform, including a draft Police Act.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Prakash Singh v. Union of India
facts.summary: Supreme Court ordered police reforms, including State Security Commissions, fixed tenures and separating investigation from law and order.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: National Human Rights Commission
facts.summary: Set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 to inquire into violations of human rights.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Sarkaria Commission
facts.summary: Commission on Centre-State relations chaired by Justice R.S. Sarkaria; it reviewed the Governor's role and Article 356 and favoured cooperative federalism.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
facts.summary: Guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment a year to every rural household whose adults volunteer for unskilled manual work.
facts.note: In force from 2 February 2006; renamed after Mahatma Gandhi in 2009.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Industrial Policy Resolution 1956
facts.summary: Reserved key industries in Schedule A for the state, making the public sector the leading force in industrial growth.

facts.subject: pub-admin
facts.name: Central Administrative Tribunal
facts.summary: Set up under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 (based on Article 323A) to hear service disputes of central government employees.
facts.verified: books: IGNOU Public Administration Paper 1; IGNOU Public Administration Paper 2
